title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 47-48
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 47 to 48 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठोऽभूर्धर्मयूपो महामखः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 47 to 48 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 47 to 48.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 47 to 48** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठोऽभूर्धर्मयूपो महामखः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठोऽभूर्धर्मयूपो महामखः । नक्षत्रनेमिर्नक्षत्री क्षमः क्षामः समीहनः ॥** **यज्ञ इज्यो महेज्यश्च क्रतुः सत्रं सतां गतिः । सर्वदर्शी विमुक्तात्मा सर्वज्ञो ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥**

He never tires, he is great and self-existent. The sacrificial post of dharma and the great sacrifice is that God of gods. The axis of the stars, lord of the constellations, patient, lean, and the one who wills. He is the sacrifice, worthy of worship, worthy of the highest worship. The rite, the long sacrifice and the refuge of the good is that God of gods. All-seeing, a liberated Self, all-knowing, the highest knowledge.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 47 to 48 mean?
faq.a: He never tires, he is great and self-existent. The sacrificial post of dharma and the great sacrifice is that God of gods. The axis of the stars, lord of the constellations, patient, lean, and the one who wills. He is the sacrifice, worthy of worship, worthy of the highest worship. The rite, the long sacrifice and the refuge of the good is that God of gods. All-seeing, a liberated Self, all-knowing, the highest knowledge.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
